Job Comparison

Enter two or more Crew Book assignments. The selected date automatically chooses the correct Crew Book revision and day-specific schedule. Swipe across the result cards to compare jobs quickly on a phone. Open the official assignment view on any card to inspect the printed train movements.

Pay Mode
Comparison results use the same human-reviewed, date-aware Crew Book data used by Crew Book Assistance. Earnings use your Engineer Pay Log pay scale and existing pay calculation engine.
Enter at least two assignments to begin.

Quick Job Lookup

Look up one regular assignment, relief crew, Yard assignment, or supported holiday assignment. The selected date applies the correct revision and any day-specific Crew Book exception automatically. For GO 202 passenger jobs, official September 8 assignment images are loaded and become viewable beginning September 8.

Quick Job Lookup uses the same verified Crew Book resolver as Crew Book Assistance and Job Comparison.

About Crew Book Assistance
Coverage: Passenger and Yard assignments are supported, with the applicable Crew Book revision selected by shift date.

Important: Crew Book information is manually maintained for convenience and reference only. Always verify your assignment using the official Crew Book in Comply365 or the official Service Planning website. Temporary programs, special events, track work, and day-to-day instructions may not be reflected. Auto-filled entries remain editable.

Reference & Help

Details that are useful when you need them, without cluttering everyday settings.

Pay Rules & RatesRate table Jul 29, 2026 • 8-hour minimum • reference details›
Minimum8 hoursNight Diff.8:00 PM–5:59 AMDaily Cert$10 normal shift
View full pay rules
Pay scale: Automatically determined from Employment Start Date using the BLET rate tables effective July 29, 2026 (60%, 80%, 90%, 100%).
Minimum: 8 hours per paid shift.
Normal OT: actual time over 8 hours.
Full-shift OT: Holiday, Short Swing, or Relief Day.
Night differential: actual time between 8:00 PM and 5:59 AM.
Meal Period: 20 minutes at time-and-one-half.
Freight Meal: 40 minutes at time-and-one-half.
Fuel Claim: 30 minutes at time-and-one-half.
Daily Cert: $10 once per normal worked shift; excluded from Special Shifts.
Trainee: 1 hour straight time per trainee, maximum 2.
Operating Without a Conductor: 8 hours straight time.
Yard Certification: 1 hour straight time per certification.
Commingle / Sheridan-Shop-House Move: each adds 8 hours straight time.
2 Classes of Service: compares the 8-hour straight-time payment with ordinary overtime attributable to the pull and uses the greater payment; the same pull is not paid both ways.
Terminal Not In Crew Book: 2 hours straight time.
Runaround Claim: 2 hours straight time plus the entered difference in earnings, all straight time.
Time on Time: variable additional straight-time payment, maximum 8:00 per shift.
Miscellaneous Penalty: user-entered description and duration paid at the selected straight-time or overtime rate.
Vacation Week: 1/52 of previous year gross earnings, minimum five basic days.
Single Vacation Day: 1/5 of the vacation-week value, minimum one basic day.
Install Engineer Pay LogAdd the app to your Home Screen or desktop.›
iPhone / iPad — Safari: Open Engineer Pay Log in Safari → ••• More → Share → Add to Home Screen → keep Open as Web App on → Add. If Share is already visible, tap it directly.

iPhone / iPad — Chrome: Open Chrome’s Share menu → Add to Home Screen → Add.

Android — Chrome: Browser menu → Install app or Add to Home screen → confirm.

Android — Firefox: Browser menu → Install or Add to Home screen → confirm.

Desktop — Chrome / Edge: Use the Install option in the address bar or browser menu when available.

Installing only changes how you open Engineer Pay Log. Your account, saved shifts, and normal cloud-sync behavior stay the same.

Welcome to Engineer Pay Log

A personal, unofficial pay-tracking tool for locomotive engineers.
Unofficial personal tracking tool. This app is not an official Long Island Rail Road, MTA, or union product. Always verify payroll questions against official records, agreements, and your pay statement.
Your data stays on this device. Shift history is stored locally in your browser. Clearing Safari website data, clearing browsing data that removes site storage, or resetting the browser/device may erase your saved shifts.
Back up regularly. Go to Settings → Backup JSON, save the file somewhere safe such as Files or iCloud Drive, and keep a recent copy. If local data is ever lost, use Settings → Restore JSON.
Set your employment start date. Engineer Pay Log uses this date to select the correct 60%, 80%, 90%, or 100% pay table for each shift.

Enable Net Pay Estimator?

A planning estimate based on your own paycheck history.

Net Pay Estimator uses the average take-home percentage from your last 10 paychecks to estimate future net pay.

Because taxes, deductions, benefits, contributions, withholding, and other payroll items vary from employee to employee, this is an estimate only and is not a guarantee of your actual paycheck.

To use this feature, enter the gross and net amounts from your 10 most recent paychecks. These amounts can be found in the BSC portal. Keeping your paycheck history current will improve the estimate.

What's New in Engineer Pay Log V9.0

September 2026

A major Crew Book and job-selection update.

  • Job Comparison: compare multiple assignments side-by-side by date, terminal, report/release times, relief days, duration, meal status, estimated earnings, and the official printed Crew Book assignment.
  • Quick Job Lookup: enter one assignment and date for a fast Crew Book summary, review the official printed assignment, or send that job directly into Job Comparison.
  • Official Crew Book images: all official assignment images for the September 8, 2026 Crew Book revision are loaded in Engineer Pay Log and will be available for viewing beginning September 8.
  • Crew Book Assistance: updated for GO 202 Revision 7, effective September 8, 2026, including the Paper Revision published to Comply365 on August 31.
  • Paper Revision visibility: where Paper Revision 8 supersedes a GO 202 page, Engineer Pay Log shows the superseding instruction and excerpt above the underlying Crew Book image until the railroad publishes an integrated replacement page.
Crew Book verification: every engineer assignment revised for the September 8 revision was manually reviewed against the official Crew Book before inclusion in Engineer Pay Log. The August 31 Paper Revision was also incorporated and manually checked.

As always, Crew Book Assistance is provided for convenience. Please verify your assignment against the official Crew Book and current railroad instructions.
